document.title: Excerpt from Record of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and George Shultz, February 22, 1988
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: The Afghanistan portion was the most difficult of a long conversation. Shultz welcomes Gorbachev's Feb 8 statement and hopes the next Geneva round will be the last. Gorbachev furiously accuses the US of changing its position on Mujahedin support since the December summit, while still prioritizing US cooperation and signing the Geneva Accords.

events.description: Gorbachev and Shultz discuss the Afghanistan settlement, the Iran-Iraq conflict and the Middle East in Moscow.
Shultz meets Shevardnadze and discusses Afghanistan and the Geneva process.
Gorbachev–Shultz conversation covering Afghanistan, the Iran-Iraq conflict, the Persian Gulf and the Middle East.
Previous-day talks between Shultz, Shevardnadze, Powell and others where a new approach on Iran-Iraq (arms embargo, special representative) was discussed.
Shultz proposed a mandatory arms embargo on a non-complying country, a set date with a ~30-day gap before the Security Council vote, and a special UN representative.
The US recently withdrew two large ships from the Persian Gulf.
Gorbachev criticized US Middle East proposals (exclusion of Syria, negative stance on the PLO) and restated the Soviet proposal for a preparatory committee of Security Council permanent members.
Gorbachev and Shultz conversation in Moscow on Afghanistan, Middle East, Iran-Iraq conflict.
Shultz talked with Shevardnadze about Afghanistan and the Geneva process.
Shakhnazarov first told Shultz of Soviet intentions to withdraw from Afghanistan.
Soviet Union issued a statement announcing a date and timeframe for troop withdrawal from Afghanistan.
US reduced its Persian Gulf naval presence by two large ships.
Shultz proposes a UN Security Council arms embargo and special representative on Iran-Iraq conflict.

relationships.detail: They hold talks in Moscow on regional conflicts including Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: Record of Conversation between M.S. Gorbachev and the US Secretary of State George Shultz. February 22, 1988, Moscow.

relationships.detail: Shultz spoke with Shevardnadze the previous day.
relationships.quote: I will not repeat everything that I said yesterday to E.A. Shevardnadze.

relationships.detail: Shakhnazarov first told Shultz of Soviet withdrawal intentions about six months earlier.
relationships.quote: Already six months ago I believed in the seriousness of your intentions, when E.A. Shakhnazarov first told me about them.

relationships.detail: Powell discussed the US Persian Gulf force posture with Shevardnadze.
relationships.quote: When E.A. Shevardnadze raised this question yesterday, I told him

relationships.detail: US Middle East proposals reached the Soviets through Matlock.
relationships.quote: We studied your proposals, which we obtained through Ambassador Matlock.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev hoped for US-Soviet collaboration in settling the Afghan question.
relationships.quote: we are hoping for collaboration with the American side in the settlement of the Afghan question.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev described new elements of collaboration between the two countries, bilaterally and in the UN Security Council, on the Iran-Iraq conflict.
relationships.quote: certain new elements in the collaboration between our countries, both bilaterally and within the framework of the Security Council, have come up

relationships.detail: The US held the chair of the Security Council at the time.
relationships.quote: The US is the chair of the Security Council right now.

relationships.detail: The Soviet Union had earlier chaired the Security Council.
relationships.quote: We did not fail in our chairmanship at the Council.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze and Shultz discussed the Iran-Iraq conflict and the UN General Secretary's role the previous day.
relationships.quote: What E.A. Shevardnadze said yesterday is true—the UN General Secretary has many other responsibilities.

relationships.detail: US naval forces were deployed in the Persian Gulf; two large ships were recently withdrawn.
relationships.quote: Recently we reduced our presence in the Persian Gulf by two large ships.

relationships.detail: Powell spoke for the US on its military presence in the Persian Gulf (role in the NSC not stated here).
relationships.quote: the accumulation of our forces in the Persian Gulf in the last 6-6 [sic] months has led to the addition of only two warships.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev stated that Iran wants a fundamentalist government to form in Afghanistan, an Iranian element in the Afghan situation.
relationships.quote: Iran wants a fundamentalist government to form in Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: Ambassador Matlock was the channel through which the US Middle East proposals reached the Soviets.
relationships.quote: We studied your proposals, which we obtained through Ambassador Matlock.

relationships.detail: Matlock conveyed US Middle East proposals to the Soviet side.
relationships.quote: We studied your proposals, which we obtained through Ambassador Matlock.

relationships.detail: The Soviet side voiced concern that US proposals took a negative position toward the PLO and Palestinian settlement, and advocated that Palestinian interests be included.
relationships.quote: your proposal reflects a negative position in relation to the Palestinian settlement, and particularly the PLO

relationships.detail: The Soviets proposed a preparatory committee including the permanent members of the Security Council to prepare a Middle East conference.
relationships.quote: we offered to start the work of a preparatory committee with the participation of the permanent members of the Security Council

relationships.detail: Shultz and Gorbachev held a recorded conversation in Moscow on 22 February 1988 covering Afghanistan, the Middle East and the Iran-Iraq conflict.
relationships.quote: Record of Conversation between M.S. Gorbachev and the US Secretary of State George Shultz. February 22, 1988, Moscow.

relationships.detail: Shakhnazarov first told Shultz about Soviet intentions on Afghanistan about six months earlier.
relationships.quote: Already six months ago I believed in the seriousness of your intentions, when E.A. Shakhnazarov first told me about them.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev refers to a prior conversation with Shultz in Washington in which he presented the Afghanistan plan.
relationships.quote: We brought our plan of action to Washington. You were the first to whom we told this plan

relationships.detail: Gorbachev suggests NSC policies feed a negative US approach to Soviet cooperation.
relationships.quote: Or maybe the policies coming from the National Security Council are at the heart of it.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says the NSC views the USSR as a state the US will come into conflict with everywhere.
relationships.quote: They still think that the Soviet Union remains and will continue to be a State with which the United States will come into conflict everywhere

relationships.detail: The USSR announced a date and timeframe for withdrawal of its troops from Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: You wanted us to make a statement about the withdrawal of our troops, to provide a date and a timeframe for the withdrawal. We did this.

relationships.detail: Both sides discuss a speedy conclusion of the Geneva agreements on Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: we would like you to contribute to a speedy signing of the Geneva agreements

relationships.detail: Shultz and Gorbachev agree a coalition government for Afghanistan will not be formed in Pakistan.
relationships.quote: Shultz: And not in Pakistan. Gorbachev: All the more so not in Pakistan.

relationships.detail: The US currently chairs the UN Security Council.
relationships.quote: The US is the chair of the Security Council right now.

relationships.detail: US naval forces are present in the Persian Gulf, recently reduced by two large ships.
relationships.quote: Recently we reduced our presence in the Persian Gulf by two large ships.

relationships.detail: The Iran-Iraq conflict is the context for the arms embargo and US naval presence in the Gulf.
relationships.quote: Iran-Iraq conflict. It looks like certain new elements in the collaboration between our countries

sources_cited: Archive of the Gorbachev Foundation, Moscow, Fond 1, opis 1 (translated by Anna Melyakova for the National Security Archive)
key_claims: Gorbachev says the USSR has set a date and timeframe for troop withdrawal from Afghanistan and wants the Geneva agreements signed quickly.
Gorbachev states the Soviet withdrawal should not be tied to the formation of a coalition government in Afghanistan.
Gorbachev and Shultz agree a coalition government should not be formed in Moscow, Washington or Pakistan; Afghans should decide.
Gorbachev denies Soviet aims of an Afghan springboard or access to warm seas and wants a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan.
Gorbachev claims Iran wants a fundamentalist government in Afghanistan.
Gorbachev says contacts are being established between Afghans unknown to both superpowers, and that influence will decline after the agreement is signed.
